items.text: Mirror of Tears
Hello, excuse me ... What is this place?
A timid face appears in the dark. Bewildered and uneasy, its owner wipes her hands on her dress, where there once was an apron.
Me? My name is Hannah. I'm a waitress at Café Central. Have we met?

items.speaker: Hannah
items.text: Oh ... I see. Sorry ...

items.speaker: Hannah
items.text: I was just at the café, working my shift. The manager told me to walk slower so that I wouldn't kick the customers' chair legs again, and then everything went dark, and I found myself in this very room!

items.speaker: Hannah
items.text: This is strange! Stranger than a novel!

items.speaker: Hannah
items.text: I was hoping you could tell me what happened—explain things to me.
She paces around, looking anxious.

items.speaker: Hannah
items.text: ... Mm? What's this?
One of her shoes hits something firm. She crouches down curiously.

items.speaker: Hannah
items.text: Oh! It's ... a painting? No ... a door?

items.speaker: Hannah
items.text: How strange that it's on the floor. Actually, it looks like the door to Café Central ...

items.speaker: Hannah
items.text: Something's written on it. It's too dark in here. I can't see. Maybe I can feel it with my fingers ... Mm?
She stops and furrows her eyebrows. She runs her fingers across the doorplate a few more times.
The name carved on it kisses the tips of her fingers. A sweet bitterness fills her heart.

items.speaker: Hannah
items.text: ... Theophil? Mr. Theophil ...?

items.speaker: Hannah
items.text: Did he play a part in the kidnapping? But why would an artist be involved in such a horrible act ...?
She mumbles to herself, her eyes rolling in the dark. She is looking for an excuse. An excuse to forgive.

items.speaker: Hannah
items.text: Or perhaps—perhaps he wants me to be his model? I'd gladly agree to it, of course ...

items.speaker: Hannah
items.text: He's so handsome and kind, and my goodness, can he paint! Any girl would agree to be his model. He wouldn't need to abduct me for that ...
A fragment of a memory comes back to her, but it's vague. Shrouded in a white haze.

items.speaker: Hannah
items.text: Oh, I think I remember!

items.speaker: Hannah
items.text: Before everything went dark, Mr. Theophil had ordered another Franziskaner. I had it on my tray, and then ...

items.speaker: Hannah
items.text: ... And then I passed out before I reached his table ...

items.speaker: Hannah
items.text: Until then, it was a perfectly ordinary day ...
The warm color of love fades from her face.

items.speaker: Hannah
items.text: Mr. Theophil looked as handsome as ever. He ordered his usual. Even Mr. Heinrich was wearing the same brown blazer ...

items.speaker: Hannah
items.text: No, no, that's not right.

items.speaker: Hannah
items.text: Something was different that day. Yes. That was the day she first met her. That was the beginning of everything.
She looks at you, trancelike. The door opens beneath her palm.
Café Central

items.speaker: Theophil
items.text: An insightful idea, miss.

items.speaker: Theophil
items.text: I've never heard of such a perspective on how to treat mental illness ... I'm very impressed.
The cream has long since melted into the Franziskaner. This conversation is much more interesting than the beverages on the table.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: See? I told you, Theophil!

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: I knew you two would get along. How could you not adore such a lovable and talkative lady?

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: The amazing Klara! We met at an auction. She has a superb taste in the arts!
Heinrich's bouts of excessive enthusiasm are a loveable weakness of his. Rather than annoy, it endears his friends to him.
He sweeps up his friend's cup and takes a huge gulp.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: Oh, by the way, Theophil. Where's your sister?

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: You said she'd be here today. I thought she'd agreed to come down to the café.

items.speaker: Theophil
items.text: Yes. She should've arrived by now. Perhaps she's been delayed on her way over.

items.speaker: Theophil
items.text: After the huge success of her debut, my little sister is the new star of Vienna. She's positively swarmed by her admirers on the streets—it's all very sweet but, as you can imagine, it can be quite troublesome.

items.speaker: Hannah
items.text: Sir, here's your coffee.
The waitress lightly places it on the table.

items.speaker: Hannah
items.text: One Vienna iced coffee and a Maria Theresa. Enjoy.
Her gaze lingers on Theophil, an eager smile upon her face. Her light brown hair is carefully tied in a curly ponytail.

items.speaker: Theophil
items.text: Thank you, Hannah. Your smile always brightens up a long afternoon.

items.speaker: Hannah
items.text: Haha ... You flatter me again, sir.
She blushes and hurriedly looks aside. This is not the first time her dear Theophil has been so sweet to her.

items.speaker: Hannah
items.text: Would you like a cake on the side? It-It's on the house.

items.speaker: Hannah
items.text: I remember you said you liked the particular lemon aroma of it ... My mother grew those lemons. She brought me some more when she last visited. Would you—

items.speaker: Theophil
items.text: Over here!

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: Oh, Isolde! My dear girl! When was it that we last met? It feels like eons!

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: It was about ... one and a half months ago?

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: Ah, how unforgivably long! Do you remember when we were younger? We saw each other every week!

items.speaker: Hannah
items.text: Theo ...

Her voice is lost among the chatter.
She quietly looks at her sweet Theophil as he gets on his feet and walks up to his sister.
He has completely forgotten about the lemons. Or, rather, he never cared about them in the first place.

items.speaker: Theophil
items.text: Why, do you think Isolde is still that little girl who followed you around?

items.speaker: Theophil
items.text: I'm afraid you're terribly mistaken, my friend! She's the biggest star of Vienna and the best and most stunning "Salome" of all time! Her admirers fill the streets, and her work has shaken the art world to its very core!
Putting both his hands on her shoulders, he basks in his pride for his sister.

items.speaker: Theophil
items.text: And all at the ripe old age of sixteen, no less! She's not some unknown actress taking minor role after minor role, nor is she one of those poets who end their miserable lives by plunging themselves into a river! No, it won't be long before she becomes the sovereign of theater!

items.speaker: Theophil
items.text: My point is, Mr. Heinrich, that it's very difficult to see her these days. But, if you can make her brother's life a little sweeter ...

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: Oh, Theophil, you crafty fellow!
Heinrich gently punches his arm. Theophil giggles as he pulls himself away from his fist.
The café is filled with their youthful laughter.
Theophil is not yet twenty. He looks young, sweet, and happy. As free as the wind.
Hannah moves her lips, nervously rubbing her hands on her apron as she tries to come up with more words to get his attention.
She notices that Isolde is looking at her and lightly shaking her head.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Thank you, but I don't feel like having a drink.

items.speaker: Hannah
items.text: It was her! Her! How could I forget? How could I forget her!?

items.speaker: Hannah
items.text: Oh, what a terrible, terrible future ...

items.speaker: Hannah
items.text: Did I hit my head? Or was it my neck? Or my legs? My waist? ... No, no, no, no ...
Small beads of sweat glisten on the tip of her nose. She checks on her neck, her back, and her limbs, making sure they are still attached to her body.
Eventually, her hands stop at her neck.

items.speaker: Hannah
items.text: It was here. Yes.
Clutching her neck with both hands, she crouches down on the floor.

items.speaker: Hannah
items.text: So much pain ... There was ... *sobs*

items.speaker: Hannah
items.text: Why? Why did it have to be me? Why not Teresa? Or Gregor?

items.speaker: Hannah
items.text: Not all who were trampled that day died. Nor those who fell to the floor ... And those who were pushed in front of the guns ... They had a quick and painless death, at least.

items.speaker: Hannah
items.text: Why me ...? Why only me ...?

items.speaker: Hannah
items.text: Why was I the only one who fell down the stairs? Why was I the only one who screamed in agony? Why was I the only one who suffered a broken neck?

items.speaker: Hannah
items.text: It shouldn't have happened—none of this should've happened! The road shouldn't have been covered in sharp gravel!

items.speaker: Hannah
items.text: Those creatures in black, with their dark slime dripping all over ... They started that demonstration!

items.speaker: Hannah
items.text: It was ... those creatures ...

items.speaker: Hannah
items.text: Monsters ...
Hannah drops her head. Tears stream down her cheeks, dripping on her palms, and pooling on the door beneath her feet.
The door is now tightly shut. The door to the café with Theophil's name on it.
On the other side, Cupid and Psyche convene.

items.speaker: Hannah
items.text: It was "The Circle." It was the speech.

items.speaker: Hannah
items.text: It was they who were responsible.
The puddle of tears beneath her feet confronts her with her own reflection. Her reflected face morphs into someone else's. Isolde.

items.speaker: Hannah
items.text: The famous opera singer with a touch of sorrow.

items.speaker: Hannah
items.text: The daughter of that mirror peddler.

items.speaker: Hannah
items.text: They killed me.

items.speaker: Klara
items.text: Hello, I'm Klara Vingler. Perhaps you've heard of "The Vingler's Mirror." That's an invention of my family.
From the other side of the table, the lady in the green dress extends a white-gloved hand.
She is leaning forward so far that she is no longer sitting in her chair. This may appear to be too eager, but the smile on her face is sincere.

items.speaker: Klara
items.text: Heinrich told me a lot about you and your brother. I'm most glad that we've finally had the chance to meet.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: I'm Isolde.
Isolde takes her hand.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: It's a privilege to make your acquaintance.
TO BE CONTINUED…
